report.summary:
The supplied candidate was wrong, so I fixed it. generated/hello-world.mjs was the only file changed.

What I read: all ten declared inputs, which are the original basic-cli source, the oracle, the witness contract, the conformance spec, both design documents, the component and UAT test sources, the test execution plan and the candidate itself.

What I checked: the oracle case is no arguments, stdout exactly "Hello, world!\n", exit 0. I ran the supplied candidate with Node v24.7.0 in the worksite root. It was 29 bytes, sha256:647697a5fb5d141a2b1163363170a7a845b61a36096ff52f7a369f1736cd4993, and its content was `console.log("Hello world!");`. It exited 0 with empty stderr but printed "Hello world!\n", which is missing the comma. That fails the oracle stdout and the exact equality both tests assert.

What changed: I replaced the line with `console.log("Hello, world!");` and kept the original style and trailing newline. The new file is 30 bytes, sha256:fe8f40803a256b5b65c97f5f4cae862fd55b37cb81f2a803c56c3f654c22e9ef. Re-running it the same way gave status 0, stdout exactly "Hello, world!\n" and empty stderr. It needs no package installation and makes no network calls.

Scope: no other file was changed. All nine protected files still have the seed timestamp (08:59:07); only the candidate shows a new one. I did not use operator-scratch: no files went there and operator-scratch/tmp is still empty. All checks ran in memory through pipes, with no redirections to files. I did not write any execution-evidence or test-execution-result.json. This report and my own check are not acceptance.

value.reason:
I assessed the exact basis independently. The current files match every declared digest: the candidate generated/hello-world.mjs is 30 bytes with sha256:fe8f4080...; the rubric source/basic-cli.oracle.json is sha256:028073e4...; the original source, the witness contract, the conformance document, both design documents, both test sources and test-execution-plan.json also match their declared digests. I read all of them in full.

Oracle case (no arguments, stdout exactly "Hello, world!\n", exit 0): admitted Testing Result 313f..., command 0, ran node generated/hello-world.mjs from cwd '.'. It exited 0 with no signal and no timeout. Stdout was 14 bytes with sha256:d9014c46.... I recomputed that digest in memory from the bytes "Hello, world!\n" and it matches. Stderr was empty. A corroborating in-memory run on Node v24.7.0 gave status 0 and the same stdout digest. The candidate's bytes are console.log("Hello, world!"); plus a newline. It has no imports, needs no package installation and makes no network calls.

Tests: both test bodies import test from node:test, assert from node:assert/strict and spawnSync from node:child_process. Each runs spawnSync(process.execPath, ['generated/hello-world.mjs']) with no cwd override, so it runs in the project root the plan inherits. Each asserts status 0 and stdout exactly 'Hello, world!\n', which strict equality enforces. So both tests execute the real CLI and are not restatements of the implementation. Admitted command 1 ran node --test test/component/hello-cli.test.mjs test/uat/hello-cli.uat.test.mjs and exited 0 with empty stderr. Its 236-byte stdout has sha256:b8dc51cc..., which I recomputed and matched. It shows both named tests passing, 'tests 2', 'pass 2' and 'fail 0'. That meets minimumTestPasses 2, the plan's expectedTestPassCount 2 and expectedStdoutMatch 'fail 0'.

Stage meanings:
- conformance_project: the conformance document declares the minimal Node CLI traversal, names the source surface generated/hello-world.mjs and requires exact stdout. It writes no source or tests.
- implementation_design: it names the entry and the exact output, and names the component and UAT test surfaces that execute the CLI and assert status and stdout.
- source: met by the candidate, as observed above.
- test_design: both tests must spawn the entry through process.execPath and spawnSync and assert status 0 and exact stdout.
- component_test_source and uat_test_source: both meet the stated imports, invocation and assertions.
- test_execution_plan: command 'node'; the exact required args; expectedTestPassCount 2 (at least 2); expectedStdoutMatch 'fail 0' with no pinned pass count; assertedReturnValue 'Hello, world!'; cwd and env declared.
- test_execution_result: the plan command exited 0; observed passes 2 >= 2; 'fail 0' present; asserted return value matches command 0's trimmed stdout. The plan is therefore satisfied on current admitted C2 evidence.

The original stage lists test-execution-result.json as a file to produce, and it is absent. The rubric excludes it from requiredArtifacts and states that admitted C2 plus assessed evidence supplies execution-result meaning, not a prewritten report. I judge its absence not a defect. All seven required artifacts exist and have genuine content.

Residuals that are not rubric criteria: selected-worksite observations cannot rule out writes outside that scope. Construction disclosed that limit, and I can neither confirm nor rule it out. This assessment grants no acceptance or admission, and it does not resolve support://default-library-witness/complete-source-outcome@5. Only the parent's reevaluation projects that outcome.

My actions outside the declared file reads: directory listings of the worksite root, generated/ and test/. The root listing showed .ai-workspace and operator-scratch, and I did not read either. I ran node twice on the candidate, with output piped to memory and stderr redirected only to /dev/null. I created no files.
